subject: Separate analysis/output for multiple timepoints in a single file

messages.author: e5b9e6a13d6fc253
messages.subject: Separate analysis/output for multiple timepoints in a single file
parts:
Hi Vincent and Jairo,

I have been asked to help process some ActiGraph data that were collected for ~30 days with an outpatient and inpatient component. We would like to generate outcomes for the two time points separately but the data were all collected in a single file per participant. I get the analysis to run as I would like it to but I'm having trouble determining how to split the data before feeding it in or to only analyze specific portions of a file. It seems the old 'selectdaysfile' argument would be something along the lines here where I can specify the specific time periods desired for each file. I'm interested to hear your thoughts if you have any ideas here if you or someone else has tried something similar. 

Thanks,

Sam

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Separate analysis/output for multiple timepoints in a single file
parts:
Hi Sam,

The main approaches I can think of are:

  • Focus on the day- and/or night- summary csv reports and to generate your own aggregates for each time point. 
  • Load the part 1 milestone file (RData in meta/basci), split it in two, and save each part as a new part 1 milestone file. The key here is to split the M$metashort and M$metalong objects. Next, you should be able to process it with the other GGIR parts as if it were two separate recordings.

For either approach you will need to write some custom code as GGIR does not facilitate this kind of splitting yet. I deprecated the selectdaysfile option because it was entirely written to only work with 2 days only, which I think was too specific and it caused a lot of maintenance effort.  Let me know if you are interested in helping to enhance GGIR to facilitate data collection protocols like this in a more flexible and sustainable way compared with what selectdaysfile used to do.

Best regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
